title: Tool-call JSON schema style guide with delta validation and error mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Tool/function calling across SDKs and hosted APIs suffers from inconsistent JSON schema authoring (naming, optional vs required patterns, discriminators) which leads to brittle validation errors that are hard for integrators to remediate. We need a single human- and machine-readable style guide + delta-validation algorithm that: 1) defines a preferred schema flavor for tool manifests, 2) produces deterministic, minimal repairable error messages with a fingerprint ID (for telemetry + docs mapping), and 3) supports graceful compatibility when rolling new tool versions to avoid breaking existing clients.

Goals: 
- Author a concise style guide (lint rules + examples) for tool JSON manifests that SDKs and the runtime can rely on.
- Implement a delta validator that compares incoming invocation payloads against a declared schema and classifies failures into recoverable hints vs hard rejects.
- Surface errors with: friendly message, recovery hint, canonical error code, stable fingerprint, and link to the docs/PR that last changed the schema.
- Add telemetry hooks (fingerprint, schema_version, route) to enable aggregating common authoring mistakes and guide future UX.

Scope (this ticket): 
- Draft the schema flavor (naming conventions, required/optional patterns, use of discriminators for unions, array semantics) and publish as a style guide doc. 
- Implement prototype linter as CLI that can run in CI for tool manifest repositories. 
- Implement server-side delta validator module (runtime only) returning structured error envelope described in acceptance criteria. 
- Wire basic telemetry output for error fingerprints (no PII).

Out of scope: automatic schema repair, SDK doc-generator changes, broader telemetry dashboards (follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Style guide published at /confluence/runtime-schema/tool-manifest-style-v1 with examples for common cases
CLI linter that flags the defined style violations and exits non-zero in CI; test-suite with >= 30 sample manifests
Runtime delta validator returns error envelope with: message, hint, code, fingerprint, schema_version, docs_link
Example mapping of 5 common authoring mistakes to friendly hints and recovery steps
Telemetry events emitted for each unique fingerprint; tests assert no sensitive fields are logged
notes: 2025-02-12: Kickoff sync — agreed to favor explicit "required fields" over permissive optional-first approach to make runtime coercion simpler.

2025-02-14: Marco implemented a draft delta comparator algorithm: computes edit-distance on field paths, then classifies missing fields as 'likely-client-bug' vs 'version-mismatch' based on schema_version header.
2025-02-17: Review from Design (Lena): suggested adding UX-friendly field name examples and a short 'migration checklist' for tool authors.
2025-02-19: Security asked for telemetry review — confirmed fingerprints must be salted server-side and no example payloads should be included in logs.

2025-02-21: Added CLI linter prototype in tooling-lint repo; current rule set covers: snake_case vs camelCase, required/optional explicitness, enum canonicalization, and discriminator presence for unions.
2025-02-24: Engineering review: prefer using a stable 12-char hex fingerprint (sha1 truncated) rather than full UUID to make telemetry buckets readable. Will document collision risk and mitigation.
2025-02-26: E2E plan: run linter in CI for internal tool repos, enable runtime validator behind feature flag for 2 weeks in staging, collect fingerprints and top-10 error classes.
Next steps: finalize style guide doc, add ~30 unit tests for comparator edge cases, open runtime PR to add error envelope, schedule staging rollout for 2025-03-03.
comments: PM (Ravi): This is high priority for customers integrating custom tools. If we can reduce 'unknown param' errors in the first 90 days, we reduce support load substantially.
Design (Lena): I'll supply 6 concrete manifest examples (good/bad/migration) by EOD 2025-02-18.
Eng (Marco): Prototype comparator lives in runtime/internal/schema_delta.go — needs tests and simplification before PR.
Security (Nora): Confirmed telemetry plan; we still need a short privacy note in the docs.
